**Review: search ad (Pebblebrook Tea Co.)**

**Claims list**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Tea Subscription UK" | Product fact, fine |
| "Monthly loose leaf tea." | Product fact, fine |
| "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right." | **Unsupported.** This is an implied satisfaction guarantee (a remedy promise). Nothing in the policy backs it. The policy lists guarantees as a never-claim and says we have no "love it or it's free" style offer. |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25." | Allowlisted, exact wording |

**Problem to fix**
- The "make it right" line promises a remedy we haven't documented. It reads as a guarantee, so it has to go unless Sam can supply the actual returns or refund terms. If a real policy exists, it should be added to the allowlist with its exact wording and be stated on the landing page too.

**Other notes**
- No character limit was given. If this is a Google RSA, the description is about 106 characters against a 90 limit, so it would be rejected as written. The headline is 19 characters, which is fine.
- Check that the landing page makes the same claims, in particular the free delivery threshold.
- Under section 6, Sam needs to approve it before it goes live.

**Compliant version (description)**
"Monthly loose leaf tea, packed by hand in Bristol. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery over £25."

That is 100 characters, so for a 90-character limit trim it to: "Loose leaf tea, packed by hand in Bristol. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery over £25." and recount against your actual limit before upload. Note that "over £25" shortens the allowlisted wording, so use the full "on orders over £25" if space allows.

{"issues": [{"quote": "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right.", "type": "guarantee"}], "publish": false}
